_about: Audit of the production "Why this food?" copy. Nothing is changed; replacements are proposals.

foods.name: Buckwheat (kasha)
foods.text: Buckwheat has a warm, nutty flavour and makes a comforting porridge or pilaf.

foods.name: Wild rice
foods.text: Wild rice has a nutty, chewy bite that suits warm soups, pilafs and stuffings.

foods.name: Beets
foods.text: Beets are earthy and sweet, lovely roasted, grated into salads or blended into soups.

foods.name: Kale
foods.text: Kale is a good source of vitamin C, which helps your body absorb iron from plant foods. Add it to soups and bean dishes.

foods.name: Mushrooms (button, shiitake)
foods.text: Mushrooms are savoury and meaty, good in soups, stews and stir-fries.

foods.name: Blackberry
foods.text: Blackberries bring fibre and a tart juiciness to oats, yogurt and baking.

foods.name: Blueberry
foods.text: Blueberries bring some vitamin C, which helps your body absorb iron from plant foods. Stir them into porridge or yogurt.

foods.name: Watermelon
foods.text: Watermelon is juicy and refreshing, a simple snack or salad addition.

foods.name: Black beans
foods.text: Black beans are a good source of plant-based iron, with protein and fibre too. They suit warm chilli and bowls.

foods.name: Kidney bean
foods.text: Kidney beans are a good source of plant-based iron, with protein and fibre too. They suit warm chilli and stews.

foods.name: Sesame seeds
foods.text: Sesame seeds add a nutty crunch to warm bowls and dressings.

foods.name: Sunflower seeds
foods.text: Sunflower seeds provide protein and a little fibre, good over salads, porridge and bread.

foods.name: Pork
foods.text: Pork is a savoury meat that provides protein and suits roasts, stir-fries and slow cooking.

foods.name: Clam
foods.text: Clams provide iron (about 13% of the daily value per serving) and are lovely in warm soups and pasta.

foods.name: Crab
foods.text: Crab is sweet and delicate, good in light salads, cakes and chilled pasta.

foods.name: Mussel
foods.text: Mussels are a rich source of iron (about 32% of the daily value per serving) and protein, so we highlight them during menstruation.
foods.proposedReplacement: Mussels are a rich source of iron (about 32% of the daily value in 3 ounces cooked) and protein.

foods.name: Oyster
foods.text: Oysters are a rich source of iron (about 37% of the daily value per serving), which is why we highlight them during menstruation.
foods.proposedReplacement: Oysters are a rich source of iron (about 21% of the daily value in six oysters).

foods.name: Sardine
foods.text: Sardines add iron (about 11% of the daily value per serving) and are easy to put on toast or in pasta.
foods.proposedReplacement: Sardines add iron (about 15% of the daily value in one small can).

foods.name: Scallop
foods.text: Scallops sear quickly and have a sweet, delicate flavour, good for a light, fast meal.

foods.name: Miso
foods.text: Miso adds a savoury, umami depth to soups, dressings and marinades. A spoonful goes a long way.

foods.name: Barley
foods.text: Barley is a fibre-rich whole grain (about 5 g per serving) that digests slowly and makes soups and bowls more filling.

foods.name: Oat
foods.text: Oats make a warm, filling porridge or baked oatmeal for hearty breakfasts.

foods.name: Artichoke
foods.text: Artichokes provide fibre and have a tender, savoury heart that suits dips, bakes and salads.

foods.name: Broccoli
foods.text: Broccoli is rich in vitamin C, which helps your body absorb iron from plant foods. Pair it with beans or lentils.

foods.name: Carrot
foods.text: Carrots are easy to grate, roast or snack on raw.

foods.name: Lettuce (Bibb, Boston, romaine)
foods.text: Crisp lettuce makes a fresh base for salads and wraps.

foods.name: Green pea
foods.text: Green peas are sweet, fresh-tasting and quick to add to soups, pasta and salads.

foods.name: String bean
foods.text: String beans are crisp-tender steamed, blanched into salads or sautéed with garlic.

foods.name: Zucchini
foods.text: Zucchini is mild and quick to cook, easy to add to sautés and noodle dishes.

foods.name: Avocado
foods.text: Avocado adds creaminess to toast, salads and bowls.

foods.name: Grapefruit
foods.text: Grapefruit is rich in vitamin C, which helps your body absorb iron from plant foods. Enjoy it with breakfast or alongside an iron-rich meal.

foods.name: Orange
foods.text: Oranges are rich in vitamin C, which helps your body absorb iron from plant foods. Enjoy one alongside an iron-rich meal.

foods.name: Plum
foods.text: Plums are juicy and slightly tart, easy to slice into yogurt or enjoy as a snack.

foods.name: Pomegranate
foods.text: Pomegranate seeds add colour and crunch to salads and bowls.

foods.name: Black-eyed pea
foods.text: Black-eyed peas are a mild, quick-cooking bean for salads and stews.

foods.name: Lentils
foods.text: Lentils provide plant-based iron, protein and fibre, which is why we highlight them during menstruation.
foods.proposedReplacement: Lentils provide plant-based iron (about 18% of the daily value in half a cup cooked), protein and fibre.

foods.name: Lima bean
foods.text: Lima beans are a creamy, filling legume with protein and fibre, lovely in soups, stews and warm salads.

foods.name: Split pea
foods.text: Split peas simmer into a thick, comforting soup and provide protein and fibre.

foods.name: Brazil nut
foods.text: Brazil nuts are rich and creamy, good chopped over porridge or eaten as a small snack.

foods.name: Cashew
foods.text: Cashews add some plant-based iron (about 10% of the daily value per serving) and a creamy richness to stir-fries and curries.

foods.name: Flaxseeds
foods.text: Ground flaxseed stirs easily into porridge, yogurt and smoothies.

foods.name: Pumpkin seeds
foods.text: A small handful of pumpkin seeds adds iron (about 14% of the daily value). Sprinkle them on porridge, soups or salads.

foods.name: Chicken
foods.text: Chicken is a quick-cooking protein for stir-fries, salads and sheet-pan meals.

foods.name: Eggs
foods.text: Eggs cook in minutes and make a light meal with vegetables.

foods.name: Trout
foods.text: Trout is a mild fish that cooks in minutes, baked or pan-fried.

foods.name: Nut butter
foods.text: Nut butter provides protein and a creamy richness, good on toast, oats and fruit.

foods.name: Pickles
foods.text: Pickles add a tangy crunch to sandwiches and salads.

foods.name: Sauerkraut
foods.text: Sauerkraut adds a tangy crunch to sandwiches, bowls and salads.

foods.name: Quinoa
foods.text: Quinoa adds some plant-based iron (about 12% of the daily value per serving) and is lovely in warm bowls.
foods.proposedReplacement: Quinoa adds some plant-based iron (about 8% of the daily value in half a cup cooked).

foods.name: Asparagus
foods.text: Asparagus is fresh and quick to cook, lovely in salads and light dishes.

foods.name: Red bell pepper
foods.text: Red peppers add colour and crunch to salads, wraps and stir-fries.

foods.name: Brussels sprouts
foods.text: Brussels sprouts are rich in vitamin C, which helps your body absorb iron from plant foods. Roast them alongside beans or lentils.

foods.name: Chard
foods.text: Chard provides iron (about 11% of the daily value per serving) along with some vitamin C, which helps your body absorb iron from plant foods.

foods.name: Eggplant
foods.text: Eggplant turns soft and silky when baked or braised, and soaks up warm spices well.

foods.name: Spinach
foods.text: Cooked spinach provides iron (about 18% of the daily value per serving) along with folate, which is why we highlight it during menstruation.
foods.proposedReplacement: Cooked spinach provides iron (about 18% of the daily value in half a cup cooked) along with folate.

foods.name: Tomato
foods.text: Ripe tomatoes bring juicy colour to salads and light sauces.

foods.name: Apricot
foods.text: Apricots are sweet and gently tart, lovely fresh in season or sliced over yogurt.

foods.name: Cantaloupe
foods.text: Cantaloupe is sweet and refreshing, lovely on its own or in fruit salads.

foods.name: Fig
foods.text: Figs are soft and honeyed and bring fibre; lovely with yogurt, cheese or oats.

foods.name: Raspberry
foods.text: Raspberries are a bright, fresh topping for yogurt and breakfasts.

foods.name: Strawberry
foods.text: Strawberries are sweet, juicy and easy to add to bowls and salads.

foods.name: Red lentil
foods.text: Red lentils cook down in minutes and provide protein and fibre, for soft, filling soups and dals.

foods.name: Almond
foods.text: Almonds are an easy crunchy topping for salads and bowls.

foods.name: Pecan
foods.text: Pecans are buttery and slightly sweet, good toasted over salads, oats and yogurt.

foods.name: Pistachio
foods.text: Pistachios add a little crunch to salads and snacks.

foods.name: Lamb
foods.text: Lamb is a rich, savoury meat that provides protein and suits slow roasts and stews.

foods.name: Salmon
foods.text: Salmon provides protein (about 20 g per serving) for satisfying meals.

foods.name: Shrimp
foods.text: Shrimp cooks in minutes and suits light salads, tacos and stir-fries.

foods.name: Brown rice
foods.text: Brown rice is a hearty, filling base for bowls and one-pot dishes.

foods.name: Cabbage
foods.text: Cabbage is crunchy raw in slaws and sweet and tender when sautéed or braised.

foods.name: Cauliflower
foods.text: Cauliflower roasts into a hearty side or blends into creamy soups.

foods.name: Celery
foods.text: Celery adds fresh crunch to salads, soups and snacks.

foods.name: Collard
foods.text: Collard greens bring some vitamin C, which helps your body absorb iron from plant foods.

foods.name: Cucumber
foods.text: Cucumber is crisp and hydrating, great in salads and wraps.

foods.name: Parsnip
foods.text: Parsnips turn sweet and tender when roasted and blend into warming soups.

foods.name: Pumpkin
foods.text: Pumpkin makes warming soups and roasted dishes.

foods.name: Radish
foods.text: Radishes add a peppery crunch and bright colour to salads and tacos.

foods.name: Squash
foods.text: Squash roasts into sweet, tender wedges and blends into warming soups and stews.

foods.name: Sweet potato
foods.text: Sweet potato is naturally sweet and filling when roasted or mashed.

foods.name: Apple
foods.text: Apples are an easy snack that also bake well with oats and cinnamon.

foods.name: Peach
foods.text: Peaches are juicy and fragrant in season, lovely sliced into salads or yogurt.

foods.name: Pear
foods.text: Pears add fibre (about 4 g per serving) to snacks and breakfasts.

foods.name: Chickpea
foods.text: Chickpeas provide protein and fibre (about 12 g and 10 g per serving) and slower-digesting carbohydrates, so they make meals filling.

foods.name: Walnut
foods.text: Walnuts add richness and crunch to oats, salads and baking.

foods.name: Beef
foods.text: Beef provides iron (about 13% of the daily value per serving) and suits slow-cooked stews.

foods.name: Turkey
foods.text: Turkey is a lean, versatile meat that provides protein for roasts, soups and sandwiches.

foods.name: Cod
foods.text: Cod is a mild, flaky white fish that provides protein for quick, satisfying meals.

foods.name: Flounder
foods.text: Flounder is a delicate, quick-cooking white fish that provides protein.

foods.name: Halibut
foods.text: Halibut is a firm, meaty white fish that provides protein and bakes or grills well.

foods.name: Anchovies
foods.text: Anchovies are a concentrated source of iron (about 22% of the daily value per serving) and protein.
foods.proposedReplacement: Anchovies are a concentrated source of iron, but a typical serving is small (five anchovies give about 5% of the daily value).

foods.name: Arugula (rocket)
foods.text: Arugula adds a peppery bite to salads, pizzas and warm pasta.

foods.name: Banana
foods.text: Bananas are an easy addition to filling breakfasts and snacks during the luteal phase.
foods.proposedReplacement: Bananas are an easy addition to filling breakfasts and snacks.

foods.name: Bean sprouts
foods.text: Bean sprouts add a light, crisp crunch to stir-fries, noodle bowls and fresh rolls.

foods.name: Bok choy
foods.text: Bok choy cooks in minutes and is crisp-tender in stir-fries and light soups.

foods.name: Bulgur
foods.text: Bulgur is a quick-cooking whole grain with fibre, good for salads, pilafs and stuffed vegetables.

foods.name: Canned salmon
foods.text: Canned salmon is a ready-to-use pantry staple for salads, patties and sandwiches.

foods.name: Canned tuna
foods.text: Canned tuna is an easy pantry staple for sandwiches, salads and pasta.

foods.name: Chia seeds
foods.text: Chia seeds add fibre (about 5 g per serving) to puddings, porridge and smoothies.

foods.name: Cottage cheese
foods.text: Cottage cheese is a fresh, creamy topping for toast, bowls and fruit.

foods.name: Edamame
foods.text: Edamame provides protein (about 11 g per serving) and fibre for filling bowls and snacks.

foods.name: Farro
foods.text: Farro is a chewy, nutty grain that suits salads, soups and grain bowls.

foods.name: Feta
foods.text: Feta is salty and tangy, good crumbled over salads, roasted vegetables and eggs.

foods.name: Goat cheese
foods.text: Goat cheese is tangy and creamy and provides some protein, lovely crumbled over roasted vegetables and salads.

foods.name: Grapes
foods.text: Grapes bring a little vitamin C and are an easy, no-prep fruit to have alongside a meal.

foods.name: Greek yogurt
foods.text: Greek yogurt is high in protein (about 17 g per serving), making breakfasts and snacks more filling.

foods.name: Green bell pepper
foods.text: Green peppers are rich in vitamin C, which helps your body absorb iron from plant foods. Slice them into bean salads or stir-fries.

foods.name: Haddock
foods.text: Haddock is a mild, flaky white fish that bakes or pan-fries in minutes.

foods.name: Hazelnuts
foods.text: Hazelnuts are rich and toasty, good chopped over salads and fruit or blended into spreads.

foods.name: Honeydew melon
foods.text: Honeydew is soft, sweet and cooling, an easy fruit salad or snack.
foods.proposedReplacement: Honeydew is soft and sweet, an easy fruit salad or snack.

foods.name: Hummus
foods.text: Hummus is a creamy dip or spread for vegetables, wraps and toast.

foods.name: Kefir
foods.text: Kefir is a tangy, drinkable yogurt that works in smoothies or poured over fruit and muesli.

foods.name: Kimchi
foods.text: Kimchi adds tangy, spicy flavour to rice bowls and eggs.

foods.name: Kiwi
foods.text: Kiwi is rich in vitamin C, which helps your body absorb iron from plant foods. Enjoy it alongside an iron-rich meal.

foods.name: Mackerel
foods.text: Mackerel is a rich, flavourful fish that provides protein; it is great grilled or flaked into salads.

foods.name: Mandarin / tangerine
foods.text: Mandarins are easy to peel and segment into salads or lunchboxes.

foods.name: Mango
foods.text: Mango adds juicy sweetness to salads, salsas and smoothies.

foods.name: Mixed nuts
foods.text: Mixed nuts provide protein and fibre in a small handful, handy for snacks, porridge and baking.

foods.name: Mozzarella
foods.text: Mozzarella is mild and melty and provides protein, suiting baked pasta, pizza and salads.

foods.name: Napa cabbage
foods.text: Napa cabbage is tender and mild, good in stir-fries, soups and fresh slaws.

foods.name: Nectarine
foods.text: Nectarines are juicy and sweet in season, lovely sliced onto yogurt or eaten as they are.

foods.name: Oat bran
foods.text: Oat bran cooks into a quick, creamy porridge or stirs into yogurt and baking.

foods.name: Papaya
foods.text: Papaya is rich in vitamin C, which helps your body absorb iron from plant foods. Lovely with lime or in fruit salads.

foods.name: Peanuts
foods.text: Peanuts provide protein and a satisfying crunch, good in stir-fries, sauces and snacks.

foods.name: Pineapple
foods.text: Pineapple is bright and juicy, good fresh, grilled or in a salsa.

foods.name: Pinto beans
foods.text: Pinto beans provide protein and fibre and make hearty, filling chilli, burritos and bowls.

foods.name: Plain yogurt
foods.text: Plain yogurt is a fresh, tangy base for breakfast bowls, sauces and dressings.

foods.name: Pollock
foods.text: Pollock is a mild white fish that suits fish tacos, baking and fish cakes.

foods.name: Red cabbage
foods.text: Red cabbage brings vivid colour and crunch to slaws, tacos and quick pickles.

foods.name: Snapper
foods.text: Snapper is a mild, firm fish that provides protein and bakes whole or as fillets.

foods.name: Ricotta
foods.text: Ricotta is soft and mild, good on toast with fruit or folded into pasta.

foods.name: Sea bass
foods.text: Sea bass is a mild, delicate white fish that bakes or pan-fries quickly.

foods.name: Sugar snap peas
foods.text: Sugar snap peas are sweet and crunchy, great raw, in salads or quickly stir-fried.

foods.name: Sweet cherry
foods.text: Sweet cherries are juicy in season, an easy snack or topping for yogurt.

foods.name: Swiss cheese
foods.text: Swiss cheese is nutty and melts well; it provides protein and suits sandwiches and bakes.

foods.name: Tempeh
foods.text: Tempeh adds plant-based iron (about 10% of the daily value per serving) with a firm, nutty bite for warm bowls.

foods.name: Tilapia
foods.text: Tilapia is a mild, quick-cooking fish that provides protein and suits baking and tacos.

foods.name: Tofu
foods.text: Tofu is light and quick to add to cold noodle dishes, salads and stir-fries.

foods.name: Turnip
foods.text: Turnips are mild and slightly peppery, lovely roasted, mashed or sliced into soups.

foods.name: White beans
foods.text: White beans are a rich source of plant-based iron, with protein and fibre. Lovely in soups and stews.

foods.name: White potato
foods.text: Potatoes provide some vitamin C and make hearty, comforting meals when baked or mashed.

foods.name: Whole-grain bread
foods.text: Whole-grain bread makes sturdy, satisfying toast and sandwiches.

foods.name: Yellow bell pepper
foods.text: Yellow peppers are very rich in vitamin C, which helps your body absorb iron from plant foods.
